Your team has enough to do. Let’s get AI doing something useful.

Council reports need writing. Decisions need tracking. The same information keeps getting copied into another document.

You can see where things could work better. Finding someone with the time to make it happen is another matter.

That’s where I come in.

I work alongside your staff to build, test, and introduce practical AI workflows within your municipality’s approved technology environment. Together, we turn a time-consuming process into something your team can use, understand, and maintain.

sections.html:
Bring me the task that makes everyone sigh.

A sensible starting point might be Council report preparation.

Your team already has templates, procedures, previous reports, and corporate standards. We can use those approved sources to build a workflow that supports consistent first drafts, flags missing information, and gives staff something useful to review.

The same approach can support other agreed priorities, including Council resolution tracking, records work, and internal administrative processes.

We choose the work around your municipality’s needs, systems, and capacity.

And yes, I love to geek out on AI. Especially when it helps someone stop copying the same information into three different places.

sections.html:
How we put it to work

Understand the process

I meet with the people doing the work, the people approving it, and your IT contacts.

We look at the templates, information sources, handoffs, and review steps involved. Then we agree on a starting point and what a successful result needs to do.

Build within your approved environment

I configure the agreed workflow using your approved tools and source material.

That includes instructions, access permissions, confidentiality boundaries, and clear points where a human checks or approves the work.

For Council reports, that means using the right template, identifying information that still needs checking, and keeping staff in control of recommendations.

Test the awkward bits, too

What happens when information is missing? A source is out of date? A draft sounds convincing but gets something wrong?

We test representative examples, gather staff feedback, and refine the workflow before it becomes part of everyday work. Any testing involving confidential information depends on your approved environment and access controls.

Hand it over properly

Your designated contact receives practical knowledge transfer and operating notes, including how to maintain templates, update source material, and manage the configured workflow.

Someone needs to own what happens after the build. We make that clear.

sections.html: In local government, records are more than just files — they are the backbone of operational continuity, transparency, and public trust. The real question is not how fast you can send something, but how fast you can find it when it matters most.
sections.text: In local government, records are more than just files — they are the backbone of operational continuity, transparency, and public trust. The real question is not how fast you can send something, but how fast you can find it when it matters most.

sections.html:
Why Records Management Matters

From bylaws and budgets to meeting minutes and permits, municipalities must ensure that critical records are searchable, accessible, and compliant with legislation including:

  • Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FOIPPA)

  • Local Government Act

  • Community Charter

This is not optional — it is legislative. And as of the 2021 FOIPPA amendments, municipalities can store data outside Canada (with risk assessments), but privacy protection responsibilities remain unchanged.

sections.html:
The AI Advantage in Records Management

From Filing Cabinets to Algorithms — AI Can:

  • Search smarter – Find records by topic, not just file name (e.g., “flood response plan” across PDFs, emails, and reports)

  • Auto-classify – Sort documents into LGMA classifications automatically

  • Summarize & suggest – Condense long policies, identify missing records, and assist with FOI responses

  • Spot trends & gaps – Analyze retention patterns, flag risk areas, and find outdated or duplicate files

sections.html:
Clear, Practical, and Compliant AI Policies

AI can be a game-changer for municipalities — but without clear policies, it can also introduce risk. A well-crafted AI policy protects public trust, ensures compliance with legislation, and gives staff the confidence to use AI responsibly.

At Catch the Beat, we guide local governments through the process of creating AI policies that are practical, future-ready, and aligned with your values.

Key Considerations When Writing an AI Policy

Clarity of Purpose

Define why AI is being used. Identify the problems it will solve or the services it will support.

Principles Over Platforms

Focus on intent, function, and outcome — not specific tools. Your policy should stay relevant even as technology changes.

Transparency Without Overload

Be open about AI use in public-facing services while avoiding unnecessary disclosure burdens.

Human Accountability

Clearly state who reviews or approves AI outputs. Make it clear that AI supports — but does not replace — human decision-making.

Privacy, Security, and Data Ethics

Follow applicable laws and best practices. Specify how data is collected, stored, used, and whether it is anonymized or sensitive.

Bias and Fairness

Commit to identifying and mitigating bias. Include a review process for continuous improvement.

Training and Literacy

AI is only as effective as the people using it. Provide staff with ongoing training and skill-building opportunities.

Review and Evolution

Set a regular review timeline (annually or biannually). Acknowledge that AI — and your policy — will evolve over time.

“We have Copilot. Now what?”

You’ve got access to the tool. Now your team needs to know what to do with it.

How do you ask a useful question? Why did it give you such an odd answer? Can it help with the report sitting on your desk? And what information should you put into it?

My workshops help municipal staff and leaders move from curiosity to practical use, with live demonstrations, hands-on exercises, and examples connected to their work.

Online and in-person workshops for local governments across Canada.

sections.html:
Bring your questions. We’ll put AI to work.

We start with the basics and build towards useful applications.

Participants learn how to give AI clear instructions, improve its responses, check its work, and recognise when human judgement needs to take over.

Think reports, documents, internal communications, and the everyday tasks that keep municipal teams busy.

And yes, we can explore building agents. That’s usually where my inner AI geek gets particularly excited.

sections.html:
What your team will learn

Understand AI without needing a technical dictionary

We cover what AI is, how it works, its opportunities and limitations, and the questions it raises about security and changes to work.

There’s space to discuss the uncertainty as well as the possibilities.

Understand the tools

Explore key AI platforms, how to assess where they fit, and practical demonstrations using Microsoft Copilot.

We connect those examples to the tools your organization approves and the access available to your participants.

Write better prompts

Practise giving AI a clear task, useful context, and a specific outcome.

Then learn how to question the response, refine the instructions, and check whether the result is usable.

“Write me a report” leaves rather a lot to the imagination. Let’s give it a better brief.

Try municipal tasks and agents

Work through practical scenarios and hands-on exercises relevant to local government.

Agent exercises introduce how focused instructions can support a defined task, with appropriate boundaries and human review.

Explore Copilot in everyday work

See how Copilot can support work in Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint, depending on your available licences and configuration.

We connect the demonstrations to documents, reporting, and communication tasks your team recognises.

Keep responsibility with the human

Responsible use runs through the learning: protecting information, checking accuracy, recognising limitations, and following your organization’s policies.

A polished answer still needs a person who understands the work.

What your team will learn Understand AI without needing a technical dictionary We cover what AI is, how it works, its opportunities and limitations, and the questions it raises about security and changes to work. There’s space to discuss the uncertainty as well as the possibilities. Understand the tools Explore key AI platforms, how to assess where they fit, and practical demonstrations using Microsoft Copilot. We connect those examples to the tools your organization approves and the access available to your participants. Write better prompts Practise giving AI a clear task, useful context, and a specific outcome. Then learn how to question the response, refine the instructions, and check whether the result is usable. “Write me a report” leaves rather a lot to the imagination. Let’s give it a better brief. Try municipal tasks and agents Work through practical scenarios and hands-on exercises relevant to local government. Agent exercises introduce how focused instructions can support a defined task, with appropriate boundaries and human review. Explore Copilot in everyday work See how Copilot can support work in Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint, depending on your available licences and configuration. We connect the demonstrations to documents, reporting, and communication tasks your team recognises. Keep responsibility with the human Responsible use runs through the learning: protecting information, checking accuracy, recognising limitations, and following your organization’s policies. A polished answer still needs a person who understands the work. Choose your workshop format Online learning series Three to four interactive sessions, each lasting one to two hours, typically delivered over four weeks. Your team has time to practise between sessions and return with questions from actual use. Includes live demonstrations, practical exercises, a custom workbook, and questions and answers in each session. Full-day, in-person workshop A practical workshop, typically running from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., with demonstrations, exercises, discussion, and a digital workbook. Content is tailored to your team’s starting point and agreed learning goals. Half-day, in-person workshop A shorter option with a focused scope agreed around your team’s priorities and available time. What your team takes away A clearer understanding of AI and its limitations. More confidence using approved tools. Practical experience writing and improving prompts. Ways to apply AI to documents, reports, and communications. A better understanding of what to check and protect. Learning materials to support continued practice. Success is seeing people apply what they’ve learned to their work and knowing when to pause, verify, or ask for help. Learning with someone who understands municipal work I’m Daphne Thomson, founder of Catch the Beat, former Director of Legislative Services, and an enthusiastic AI geek. I’ve supported more than 20 local governments across Canada through AI guidance, training, and transformation work. I love showing people what’s possible. I love it even more when someone says, “Oh! I could use that for the thing I’ve been putting off.” Let’s make this useful for your people. Tell me who’s attending, which tools you have, and what your team would like help with. AI might help prepare the report. It won’t answer to your residents.

Council will.

As AI becomes part of municipal work, elected officials need to understand what it can do, where it can go wrong, and what responsible oversight looks like.

I help Councils build that understanding through practical, plain-language sessions grounded in local government.

You’ll leave better prepared to ask questions, consider safeguards, and provide informed direction.

sections.text: Plan Your Council Session

sections.html:
What should Council be asking?

An AI policy comes forward. A software purchase includes AI features. A report proposes using an agent to support a municipal service.

What does Council need to know before supporting the next step?

We work through questions such as:

  • What problem are we trying to solve?
  • What information will the tool use, and who can access it?
  • How will staff check the results?
  • Where is human approval required?
  • How will we know whether it is helping?
  • Who remains accountable when something goes wrong?

You don’t need to know how to build an AI agent to ask a very good question about one.

sections.html:
What we cover

AI explained in human language

What AI is, where it can help, and why it sometimes produces an answer that sounds certain but is wrong.

Municipal examples make the opportunities and limitations easier to understand.

Council’s role and administration’s responsibilities

How Council sets policy direction and provides oversight, and how administration manages implementation and day-to-day operations.

We explore how to support responsible adoption while respecting those roles.

Privacy, records, and public trust

What AI use means for confidential information, municipal records, transparency, accuracy, bias, and fair treatment.

The discussion connects these issues to the decisions and services residents rely on.

Policies, budgets, and procurement

Questions Council can ask when reviewing proposed uses, vendors, safeguards, funding requests, and performance reports.

The aim is to make those conversations more informed and useful.

Elected officials’ own use of AI

Boundaries for using AI in your Council role, including confidential and in-camera information, checking outputs, and protecting working relationships with staff.

AI can support your preparation. Your judgement and responsibility remain yours.
